summary_html: Family agrees to a **voluntary service plan**—counseling, substance-use treatment, parenting classes—designed to correct conditions without court compulsion. Federal law prioritizes family preservation through prevention and support services.
authority_html:
- **Family First Prevention Services Act (FFPSA)** — prevention services and kin support framework  
- **SSA Title IV-B (42 U.S.C. §§ 620–629m)** — child-welfare services and family-preservation funding

primary_citations.citation_text: District of Columbia - D.C. Code Title 4, Chapter 13, Subchapter I, Part C (Child and Family Services Agency) — § 4-1303.04 services authorized; custodial placement; removal of child

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: United States District Court for the District of Columbia
key_cases.holding: After trial the court found the District's child welfare system violated federal and District statutory and constitutional requirements at nearly every stage, including a consistent failure to provide services or make reasonable efforts to prevent placement, and ordered systemic relief.
key_cases.relevance: It found that voluntary and preventive services were largely unavailable in the District, so 'voluntary services' often existed only on paper.
key_cases.quote: the Court finds that defendants have consistently failed to provide services or otherwise use “reasonable efforts” to prevent placement

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: As applied, Washington's broad third-party visitation statute violated the mother's due process rights because the trial court gave no special weight to the presumption that a fit parent acts in her children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: It is the constitutional reason a voluntary service plan must rest on parental agreement rather than state substitution of judgment.
key_cases.quote: there is a presumption that fit parents act in the best interests of their children

key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: Reasonable efforts require CFSA to identify the barriers to reunification and to refer the parent to appropriate services addressing them; CFSA satisfied that duty here and the change of permanency goal from reunification to adoption was affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: It holds that a social worker cannot compel treatment but must ensure the parent has access to it.
key_cases.quote: requires the District to identify the barriers to reunification and prepare a case plan by recommending appropriate services designed to address the needs of each child and family

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: Not later than 72 hours, excluding Sundays
